raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been doing wheat-maize for 15 years on these 6 mu, so most of it I do by feel now, but I still pay attention to what's changing.

**Wheat (planted last October, harvesting this June)**

My wheat went in around October 10th last fall, like always — any later and the cold stunts it. I used Jimai 22, the variety most folks around here use. Saved some seed from last year, bought a little fresh to mix in, about 15 kg/mu at sowing.

For fertilizer on wheat I follow what's worked: about one bag (40 kg) of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base before planting, then topdress urea at greenup in March. The extension fellow says 15 kg N per mu is enough but I usually push it a bit — maybe 18 total — because my soil's been worked hard and I don't want yellow leaves at jointing. If the wheat looks good and green in March I'll hold back on the topdress; if it looks weak I add another scoop.

Irrigation — I'll water 3 times with the well: once at greenup, once at jointing if it's dry, and once at grain filling. Can't skip the grain filling one, that's where the weight comes from. Each watering costs me maybe 40 yuan/mu in electricity, so I don't do extras.

I'll spray herbicide once in spring for the broadleaf weeds, and watch for aphids near heading — usually need one insecticide spray.

Expecting around 450 kg/mu if the weather holds. Last year I got 470, year before that only 380 because of the late frost.

**Maize (planting mid-June right after wheat)**

As soon as the combine clears the wheat I've got maybe 5 days to get maize in — can't waste a day. I'll no-till plant directly into the stubble with a hired planter (costs me 25 yuan/mu but saves the turnaround). Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, buying fresh every year because it's hybrid.

For maize fertilizer I put down a bag of compound at planting and topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (about 40 days in). Total N around 16 kg/mu. With the summer rain I usually only need to irrigate once or twice — if July is dry I'll water at tasseling, that one's critical.

One herbicide spray right after planting, and if I see the corn borer moths I'll spray once. Not going to waste money on preventive sprays.

Expecting maybe 500 kg/mu. My maize usually does better than my wheat.

**The family and budget**

Seven of us in the household but really only me and my wife do the field work full-time — my older son works construction in Handan, younger kids are in school, my parents help with small jobs. 6 mu is manageable with family labor, don't need to hire anyone except the planter operator.

Money is tight. Fertilizer prices went up again this year, so I'm watching every yuan. If I had more cash I'd probably add potash, but compound fertilizer is what I can afford.
